change_reason: Protocol v3 (proposed decision 0130, issue #340, part of #163) widens the comparison from three targets to eight at the operator's 2026-11-07 direction as the issue states it: MailSlurper, smtp4dev, Inbucket and GreenMail join Mailpit and MailHog, and Alkemio's patched MailSlurper image is reported as its own labelled row. It copies protocol v2's corpus, throughput and wait profiles, budgets, resources and statistics unchanged and adds only the targets, each target's storage, cap and wait-method facts, a per-target capabilities record and a per-product scope. It is a separate run with a separate denominator: the 2026-10-30 v2 collection stays as recorded, and no table or statistic merges a v2 cell with a v3 cell. Its bytes are not frozen: four rows have no verified pin yet (MailSlurper, smtp4dev, GreenMail and Alkemio's image) and the Inbucket pin carries two open facts, so it is a draft whose unresolved list names every missing fact.

observation.justification: The common client path: the same search poll every target gets, at the interval frozen for the competitors.

Common-client polling over the captured API's search endpoint (/api/v1/search): a complete scan at once, then one 100 ms after each completed scan, until the cutoff; a match first seen after the cutoff is late (censored). Selected as the labelled common method (proposed decision 0093 §4), not the best available: the reviewed websocket source (sources.lock.json) establishes no lossless wait.

claim.statement: Measures the digest-checked executables named in products, launched with the lock's fixed launch. For an official target each release tag's commit is attributed source context only: nothing ties an executable to it, so no built-from, equivalence or same-build claim is made. Mailpit, MailHog, MailSlurper, smtp4dev and Inbucket are official artifacts; GreenMail is an official jar run on a pinned JRE; the alkemio-mailslurper row is a third-party patched image's extracted binary, run natively and never counted as an official competitor row, and the swarmail candidate is neither. MailSlurper, smtp4dev and Inbucket tag their releases lightweight, which carries weaker source evidence than an annotated tag. Throughput and observed visibility within the declared deadline are all that is claimed: no durability, no accept==stored and no equivalence. Storage is the unmatched profile and resources the unenforced local profile; both are stated in every report. Targets without a verified server search are scanned completely and filtered on the client, and GreenMail is read over POP3; both are labelled per row.

unresolved: mailslurper: no verified pin: the release-1.15.0 Linux executable's SQLite storage is a CGO_ENABLED=0 stub that dies at startup (a real bounded launch on 2026-11-07), and no database server or cgo build was supplied; its tag is lightweight and the executable reports v1.14.1

smtp4dev: no verified pin: the release archive has no license document (49 members, none a license) and none was captured, so no license can be pinned; its default retention (100 per mailbox, from the captured appsettings.json) is overridden by the launch, which was corrected from its --help and never run as a server

inbucket: tagged_source is unresolved: the captured ref names the commit directly (a lightweight tag) and no git_tree of that commit was captured; the pin's member field holds only the leaf name inbucket of the archive member inbucket_3.2.0_linux_amd64/inbucket
inbucket: best_wait is unresolved: no source, route or real-binary observation of a wait exists, and its server_search and native_wait capabilities are not_inspected

greenmail: no verified pin: the captured release release-2.1.15 lists no assets and no document records where the jar was fetched, so it cannot be bound to an official release asset; its tag is annotated and no git_tag or git_tree was captured; its JRE runtime pin and the runtime-list ruling (decision 0130 section 6) wait on that

alkemio-mailslurper: no verified pin: its executable needs the musl loader /lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1, which no supplied bytes carry, and the full index digest sha256:55029f542c19d0fe570450dc5a30f54dbdb24d9113a6e0e1bf96da000ebd0838 is only the dispatcher's recorded line, with no index, manifest or layer bytes supplied
capabilities of mailslurper, smtp4dev, greenmail and alkemio-mailslurper are not_inspected: they have no pin to cite
native waits of mailpit and mailhog stay not_inspected: the reviewed websocket sources establish no lossless wait, and best-wait is not declared

decoders for mailslurper, smtp4dev and alkemio-mailslurper are proved only on authored fixtures: no real-binary round trip has run for them; the inbucket decoder and the greenmail POP3 reader were proved against the real executables in unmeasured tests only
